name: OGE Energy
headline: The only electric utility for about 913,000 customers in Oklahoma and western Arkansas.
what_short: Electric utility in Oklahoma and Arkansas
what_it_does: OGE Energy owns OG&E, a vertically integrated electric company that generates, transmits and delivers power to about 913,000 customers in Oklahoma and western Arkansas. State regulators set its rates: 88% of 2025 electric revenue comes under the Oklahoma Corporation Commission, 7% under Arkansas, and 5% under the federal regulator FERC.
why_it_passed: Nobody builds a second electric grid alongside OG&E's 30,000-square-mile network (net plant $12.7 billion), and customers have no cheaper supplier for their home's wires.
Regulators grant it a set return on the money it invests, about 9.5% on equity in recent cases.
It earned 6.5% on its total capital in 2025, and about 6.7% on the capital it added since 2020.
Its earnings can be pictured ten years out, because they follow the capital it is allowed to invest.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what OGE may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. The analysis values the shares at about $27 against a price of $48.41, nearly 80% above, and the cash left for owners is only about 3% of the price, against 5.33% on a 30-year US Treasury bond.
watch: Regulators often grant much less than asked: it asked for $332.5 million in Oklahoma in 2023 and was granted $126.7 million.

Spending on the grid and plants ran at 2.1 times depreciation in 2021 to 2025, and the 2026 to 2030 plan is $7.3 billion, so cash left for owners was negative every year and the gap was filled with new debt and shares.
Rating agencies' outlooks on its debt are negative, and rural electric cooperatives contest its right to serve large new loads.
